title: Git Internals: Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision notes on how Git stores data: the four object types, SHA hashes, refs and HEAD, the index, packfiles, how a commit is built, and the plumbing commands to inspect it all.

chapters.title: The Object Database Mental Model
points: Git is a content-addressable store: key = SHA-1 (40 hex chars) of the content, value = the object, kept in .git/objects/ab/cdef...
Four object types: blob (file bytes, no name), tree (directory listing), commit (snapshot pointer + metadata), tag (annotated, named pointer)
Object ID = SHA-1 of header 'type size\0' + content, so identical content always gives the same hash and is stored once
Objects are immutable: changing a byte changes the hash, so 'editing' always creates a new object
Mental model: a commit points to a tree, a tree points to blobs and sub-trees, and commits point to parent commits to form the DAG

chapters.title: Blobs, Trees, Commits and Tags
points: Blob stores only file contents; the filename and mode live in the parent tree entry, so a rename costs no new blob
Tree entry format: mode, type, hash, name (100644 file, 100755 executable, 120000 symlink, 040000 tree)
Commit holds: tree hash, parent hash(es), author, committer, message; a root commit has no parent and a merge commit has two or more
Lightweight tag is just a ref to a commit; annotated tag is a real tag object with tagger, date and message (git tag -a v1.0 -m 'msg')
Unchanged subtrees are reused by hash between commits, so a snapshot only adds new objects for what changed

chapters.title: Refs, HEAD and the Index
points: A branch is a file in .git/refs/heads/<name> holding one commit hash; creating a branch writes 41 bytes
HEAD is normally a symbolic ref ('ref: refs/heads/main'); detached HEAD means it holds a raw commit hash, and new commits can be lost once you switch away
The index (staging area, .git/index) is a binary file listing path, mode, blob hash and stat info for the next commit
git add hashes the file, writes the blob into the object store, then updates the index entry
git status compares HEAD vs index (staged) and index vs working tree (unstaged); git reflog shows where HEAD and refs have been, which is how lost commits are recovered

chapters.title: How a Commit Is Built and Packed
points: Commit flow: git add writes blobs and updates the index, git write-tree turns the index into tree objects, git commit-tree creates the commit object, update-ref moves the branch

Sample plumbing build: echo hi | git hash-object -w --stdin; git update-index --add --cacheinfo 100644,<sha>,a.txt; git write-tree; git commit-tree <tree> -m msg; git update-ref refs/heads/main <commit>
A commit hash covers its tree, parents, author, dates and message, so changing any ancestor rewrites every descendant hash (why rebase and amend change history)
Loose objects are zlib-compressed one file each; git gc or git repack bundles them into a packfile (.pack plus .idx index)

Packfiles store similar objects as deltas against a base object, which is why a repo's size grows far slower than the sum of its snapshots; git gc also prunes unreachable objects after the expiry period

chapters.title: Plumbing Commands and Common Mistakes
points: git cat-file -t <sha> prints the type, -s the size, -p pretty-prints the content; e.g. git cat-file -p HEAD shows the commit
git hash-object <file> prints the hash; add -w to actually write the blob into the object database
git ls-tree HEAD lists the root tree; -r recurses into subtrees; git ls-files -s shows the index entries
git rev-parse HEAD resolves a name to a full hash; git show-ref lists all refs; git verify-pack -v <idx> inspects a pack
Mistake: thinking a branch contains commits (it only points to one tip); the commits live in the object database and survive branch deletion until gc
Mistake: running git gc --prune=now or deleting .git/objects files by hand, which destroys the recovery path via reflog
Mistake: assuming SHA-1 hashes are a security signature; they identify content, only signed commits and tags prove who made them

chapters.title: Git Internals Cheat Sheet
points: Object types: blob = file bytes, tree = directory, commit = snapshot + parents, tag = annotated name; stored at .git/objects/xx/yyyy
Inspect: cat-file -t / -s / -p <sha>, ls-tree -r HEAD, ls-files -s, rev-parse HEAD, show-ref
Write: hash-object -w, update-index --add --cacheinfo, write-tree, commit-tree, update-ref
Refs: .git/refs/heads/*, .git/refs/tags/*, HEAD (symbolic ref or raw hash), logs in .git/logs for reflog
Storage: loose zlib objects, git gc / repack makes .pack + .idx with delta compression; unreachable objects are pruned after expiry
